candidates.rationale: A month of purely idiosyncratic (market-demeaned) price pressure is dealer inventory that gets paid back while the long trend is intact, but in a broken long trend the same move is slow diffusion of bad news and continues, so the stock's own trend regime sets the sign of the monthly reversal.

A stock whose daily returns have been negatively autocorrelated for a quarter is being priced by inventory-bearing liquidity providers, so last week's move is compensation due back; where autocorrelation is positive the same move is gradual information diffusion and persists.

How far price runs above the open versus below it, averaged over a quarter, measures the direction of intraday execution pressure from institutional parent orders that are worked over many days, and that imbalance keeps pushing after each close.

When the floor of the daily range rises faster than the ceiling, buyers are absorbing supply without paying up (accumulation that resolves upward); a ceiling falling faster than the floor is distribution into bids.

Dating the nine-month extremes (low long ago, high recent) measures an intact advance from rank information only, immune to the single jump days that dominate return sums, and turnover rising against the name's own long-run level confirms real participation rather than drift on thin volume.

A stock whose intraday range expands on down days is held by forced or levered sellers, so its price carries a transient liquidation discount that is repaid, while names whose range expands on up days are being chased and give the premium back.

Firms with long operating cycles (low asset turnover) resolve news slowly, so their five-month trends stay underreacted to and drift, while fast-cycle firms impound the same news immediately and their trends overshoot and revert.
A price trend backed by cash-based earnings keeps getting confirmed by later reports, while the identical trend in a name whose earnings lean on accruals reverses as those accruals unwind.

Scoring today's short-horizon trend against the same stock's own five months of trends flags transient demand rather than the persistently high-beta names a cross-sectional momentum rank picks up, and self-relative extremes revert.

The same two-month move costs far more impact in a name that trades thin, and impact is transitory, so illiquid movers hand it back while the identical move in a liquid name is information and persists.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. The only strong accept (4.00) was long-window price structure: position under a 189-day high times 126-day return vol. Spend more of the round in the medium/slow niche with windows over 100 days.
  2. The second fast/price_volume/low accept scored 0.090, so that slot is filled with near-nothing. Aim to displace it, and stop re-deriving path-efficiency / signed-sum-over-abs-sum ratios.
  3. One expression was submitted twice in the same round. Diff each proposal against the round's own proposed list, not just the archive, before submitting.
  4. $dollar_volume appeared once, as a same-day multiplier on $return, and failed. If volume is retried, use it over 60+ day windows as a scaler or conditioner instead.
  5. Return aggregations over 3 to 10 day windows all failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.29 to 0.81) even when divided by a 45 to 84 day vol; every return-sum that was accepted used a window of 42 days or longer.
  6. 252-day lookbacks came back at ~0.87 coverage on both $roa and $dollar_volume, so 252 is not survivable on this island; 189 was the longest window that passed, treat it as the ceiling.
  7. Two fundamental fields multiplied together ($roe * $book_per_share) landed exactly on the coverage line, while the fundamental that scored 2.108 used one field over a price field; keep to at most one fundamental per expression.
  8. Four crossovers picked a bare $volume as one parent and inherited a single node; pick parents that both carry a multi-node subtree, not a raw field leaf.
  9. Retuning one constant or one price field of an archived expression is not novelty: EMA 42 for EMA 10, range window 63 for 21, and $high for $close inside TS_MAX were all caught as subtree overlap or rho >= 0.91.
  10. Changing the normalizer under an unchanged numerator gave rho 0.996 (TS_STD versus TS_SUM(ABS) over TS_SUM($return, 63)); novelty has to come from the numerator's field or sign structure, not the denominator.
  11. The stochastic / range-position template ($close against TS_MIN and TS_MAX of the same window) lost three proposals this round to duplicate and correlation; stop sampling that shape here.
  12. Fitness clustered at 1.97 to 3.64 where two widely separated windows were ratioed or two CS_RANKs of different signal families were multiplied; single-window distance-from-high and IF-gated regime switches scored ~0.42 and are already covered.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
